result.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the filter is `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)` — an exact, case-sensitive comparison, and the guest input is never lowercased (unlike the blacklist, which is lowercased). So 'User@Example.com' vs 'user@example.com' both pass, creating duplicate attendee rows via createMany; the frontend Zod schema also uses exact Set equality, so it doesn't catch this either. The mechanism is fully verifiable in the diff and is a real correctness defect.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the dedupe logic for new guests is `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)` and blacklist check is `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` without normalizing `guest`/`attendee.email` casing. Since the input schema (`z.string().email()`) does not lowercase, this can treat `User@Example.com` and `user@example.com` as different and allow duplicate attendee creation via `createMany`, leading to compounded calendar/email updates.
